proposals.observation: 2 of 2 quiz starters reached the email_shown step and neither completed — 0% completion rate across 48h. The drop is specifically at the email gate, not earlier in the flow, which points to trust friction at the moment of data capture rather than disengagement with the content.
proposals.proposal: Soften the email gate copy to make the value exchange explicit and lower-stakes. Replace a generic 'Enter your email to see your results' pattern with a line that names what the person gets and why it is worth it, using ICP-resonant language about honest self-knowledge rather than lead-gen framing.
proposals.current_text: Enter your email to see your results
proposals.new_text: Where should we send your results? You'll get a short, grounded read on the money pattern this points to — no pitch, just the honest picture.
proposals.impact: Lifts email-gate conversion from 0%, directly unblocking the only active acquisition funnel

proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post GitHub Actions workflow failed at 06:30 on 2026-05-17. The queue holds 9 posts so content exists, but the automation is not publishing it. This is a silent revenue-adjacent failure: SEO compounding and ICP trust-building both depend on daily cadence, and today's post did not ship.
proposals.proposal: Add a single fallback step to the workflow that posts a Slack or email notification to Joel when the run fails, so the failure is no longer silent. As a same-file fix, amend the workflow YAML to add an 'on failure' notify step pointing at a webhook already present in the repo's secrets (SLACK_WEBHOOK or similar). This is one file, one diff, and surfaces the problem within minutes rather than 24h.
proposals.new_text:
- name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        run: |
          curl -s -X POST "${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}" \
            -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
            --data '{"text":"⚠️ Daily Blog Post workflow failed — queue has posts but nothing shipped. Check run logs."}'
proposals.impact: Turns a silent daily failure into a same-hour alert, protecting content cadence and SEO compounding

proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate of the three sequences at 50% (4 opens from 8 sends), yet it is the smallest segment. This is the audience most aligned with the ICP — people who earn but don't build often exhibit vigilance patterns: they watch money closely but avoid committing it. The sequence is being read but there is no data suggesting it converts to a next step.
proposals.proposal: Add a single low-friction CTA sentence to the final email in the Money Vigilance sequence that names the quiet tension vigilance-pattern readers feel and invites them to a short conversation. Frame it as an honest reckoning rather than a sales moment — one line, one link.
